title: Using Your Voice at Work
text: How to speak up confidently, respectfully, and fairly in the workplace — for yourself and for others.
cdi_links: 4.C.04 Being willing to speak up for themselves and others

title: Introduction
bullets: People need to speak up in the workplace to ask for support, raise concerns, or stand up for fair treatment
Using your voice professionally and respectfully is a key career skill
Advocating for yourself and others builds positive workplace relationships
Speaking up can create fairer, safer, and more respectful environments

title: Success Criteria
bullets: I can explain what self-advocacy means
I can give examples of workplace advocacy
I can explain how respectful communication creates positive change

title: Key Words
bullets: Self-Advocacy – Speaking up for your own needs, rights, or goals
Workplace Relationships – The way people interact, communicate, and support each other at work
Professional Voice – Communicating clearly, confidently, and respectfully in a work setting

title: Starter Activity
bullets: Think of a situation where staying silent might cause a problem
Who do you know that speaks confidently and respectfully for themselves?

title: Advocating for Yourself
bullets: Self-advocacy involves asking for what you need, setting boundaries, raising concerns appropriately, and communicating respectfully
Examples include requesting reasonable adjustments, feedback, or support, and explaining when something feels unfair or unsafe

title: Speaking Up for Others
bullets: Advocating for others supports fairness, inclusion, and respect in the workplace
This may include challenging unfair treatment, supporting a colleague, or reporting serious concerns
UK Equality Act 2010 protects individuals from discrimination based on age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, and other characteristics
Using your voice appropriately helps create safer and more inclusive workplaces

title: Real-World Examples
bullets: Employees campaigning for fair pay or safer working conditions
Whistleblowers reporting illegal or unsafe practices
Workers supporting colleagues facing discrimination
Staff raising concerns through formal workplace procedures
These actions require confidence, courage, and professional communication

title: Using Your Voice at Work
sentence: Speaking up in the workplace helps create a more ______ environment and supports ______ treatment for everyone.

title: Key Takeaways
bullets: Using your voice confidently and respectfully is essential for fairness, safety, and positive workplace relationships
Self-advocacy and supporting others helps create inclusive environments and builds professional skills
